Name of the device: Owner tenant of the device (usually Admin)

How the server's BGP AS number is determined. **Assign automatically** takes the next AS number from the System ASN range; **Enter manually** takes an explicit value; **ASN-Agnostic** leaves assignment to the device, and the connected switches accept any AS number the server presents except the switch's own. ASN-Agnostic is offered only on servers with the Generic role and is honored only on NVIDIA Cumulus Linux switches — see :doc:`Unmanaged EVPN VTEP </unmanaged-evpn-vtep>`.
Main loopback IP address for the device. A subnet with purpose set to *loopback* needs to be defined in IPAM for the current site; applicable to servers with EVPN-VTEP role
Management IP address for the device. A subnet with purpose set to *Management* needs to be defined in IPAM for the current site; applicable to servers with EVPN-VTEP role
Tells Netris whether the server is an agentless generic node (most use cases, including an unmanaged EVPN VTEP), a CloudStack hypervisor, or an EVPN-VTEP (EVPN-on-Host) node.

Total number of physical ports on the server, including production interfaces, management interfaces (e.g., iDrac/IPMI), DPU ports, BMC, and front panel ports. A typical DGX node has 8 East-West ports, 2 North-South ports, and 2 or 3 management ports, including the server and DPU BMCs. Netris recommends setting this value to at least 16 ports.
Quantity of DPUs on the server operating in Zero-Trust mode. Most deployments have 1 DPU per server.

Custom attributes in JSON format. Typical use cases include providing East-West host-side IP addressing and routing information, and validating topology. This field is also used by the NVIDIA UFM and NMX-C plugins to store additional information such as GUIDs and GPU IDs for the server node.
Custom metadata that can be used for built-in functions or user-created API automations.
Used for describing physical connections between switches, servers, and SoftGates
